name: design_beam
description: SIZE / DESIGN a rectangular beam: given factored demands V_u (kN) and M_u (kN·m) and the maximum allowed section max_b × max_h (mm), returns the CHEAPEST feasible design (b, h, d, f'c, longitudinal bars, stirrup bar + spacing) found by a deterministic full-grid search, plus the top-5 ranked alternatives and a reason when nothing fits. Section grid: b from 250 to max_b step 50, h from 350 to max_h step 50; f'c from the fixed grade list; longitudinal steel D16/D19/D22/D25 × 1-6 bars; stirrups D10/D12/D13, 2 legs. Checks: shear (simplified Vc row (a), φVn ≥ Vu, Vs ≤ 0.66·√f'c·b·d, Av ≥ Av,min §9.6.3.3, 100 ≤ s ≤ s_max §9.7.6.2.2), flexure (φMn ≥ Mu via flex_capacity, A_s ≥ As,min §9.6.1.2). Objective: minimum total cost per metre (concrete + longitudinal steel + stirrup steel; placeholder unit rates, configurable). Use this tool instead of shear_capacity/flex_capacity when the question asks to design/size/section a beam, pick bars, or find the cheapest/most economical beam for given Vu and Mu — never iterate candidate sections yourself, one call returns the optimum.

V_u.description: Factored shear demand at the critical section (kN)

M_u.description: Factored moment demand (kN·m); required — pass 0 for a flexurally trivial demand

max_b.description: Maximum allowed beam width b (mm); grid iterates 250 → max_b step 50

max_h.description: Maximum allowed beam depth h (mm); grid iterates 350 → max_h step 50

cover.description: Clear cover to the stirrup (mm); d = h − cover − φ_long/2, stirrup diameter folded into the cover margin

rate_conc.description: Concrete unit costs $/m³ keyed by f'c grade; default {20:120, 25:125, 30:130, 35:135, 40:140} (placeholder rates, not real prices); missing grades fall back to the defaults

rate_steel.description: Steel unit cost $/kg (placeholder, not a real price)

output.unit: design dict (b, h, d, f'c, bars, spacing, capacities, cost)
